title: Edwards on beauty
hook: Jonathan Edwards saw God as the source of all beauty

segments.voice: Yesterday, Pascal and the reasons of the heart. Your line was the heart has reasons. What did your heart know that your head couldn't prove? Day one thousand two hundred sixty.

A young man walks alone in his father's pasture, looking up at the sky and the clouds. Later he wrote that something had changed in how he saw everything. God's glory seemed to show in the sun and moon and stars, in the clouds, the grass, the flowers, even in thunder, which used to frighten him. His name was Jonathan Edwards, a New England preacher. This week has been a row of thinkers: Julian's mother love, Luther's freedom and his cross, Calvin's providence, Hooker's reason, Pascal's heart. It ends with beauty.

For Edwards, beauty isn't decoration added on top of religion. It sits close to the center. God, he taught, is beautiful in himself, and every lovely thing in the world is a kind of echo or shadow of that beauty. A sunset is borrowed light. When Edwards tried to say what real goodness is, he talked about harmony: beings in loving agreement with one another, the way notes agree in a chord. Holiness, in his eyes, wasn't grim. It was lovely. He found that in the Bible. Psalm 19: "The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork." Psalm 96: "O worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness." And the one request in Psalm 27, a psalm of David: "One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD." To behold. Not to argue about, not to prove. To look. Edwards could preach fiercely about judgment. The same man wrote about God's glory in snow and sky and a field of flowers. Both were real to him. And for Edwards, the change he called conversion was something like gaining a new sense, a taste for that beauty. He compared it to honey: you can hear honey described all day, but you only know its sweetness by tasting it. Edwards wanted his hearers to taste the honey, not just hear it described.
screen: `TO BEHOLD THE BEAUTY OF THE LORD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: notice something beautiful. Settle, and breathe. Let your eyes find one beautiful thing nearby, or one you can call up from memory: light on a wall, a tree outside the window, a face you love, the sound of rain. Don't analyze it. Behold it, the psalm's word. Stay with it longer than feels normal. When your mind wanders off, come back to it. If you pray, you can let it lead you toward the one Edwards believed it echoes. The bell holds the time.
Edwards on beauty. Jonathan Edwards's teaching that God is beautiful, and that every beauty in the world reflects that beauty.
Your line: God is beautiful. Today, stop once for something beautiful and give it a full ten seconds before you move on. Day one thousand two hundred sixty.

howItsDone: Christians who read Jonathan Edwards, especially in Reformed and evangelical churches, speak of God's beauty and glory; across churches, Christians pray the Psalms of creation and worship "in the beauty of holiness" through music, art and attention to the natural world.

fork.setup: you're young Edwards, alone in your father's pasture. thunder used to terrify you. now a storm rolls in. what happens?
options: you run for cover, terrified as ever.
you watch, and the storm seems to show God's glory.
you don't notice it at all.
fork.reveal: Edwards wrote that after the change in him, even thunder, which once frightened him, seemed to speak of God's glory.
